Big news for peptide compounding.

HHS has released a draft enforcement discretion policy for certain peptides used in 503A compounding, following the FDA advisory committee’s recommendation that six peptides be added to the bulks list.

The reality is that interest in peptides never went away. Many consumers simply shifted to research use only websites and unregulated sources while policy caught up.

This announcement creates a clearer path back to licensed pharmacies, healthcare providers, and prescription-based care.

We’ve been preparing for this for months. Now we get to put that work to use.

Big thanks to AAPM @pep.med for the work they put in to help get this over the line.

Full update at the link in bio.

Jean Cunningham, PharmD, BCPS, Senior Director of Medical Affairs at Empower Pharmacy, recently spoke with BlackDoctor.com about why perimenopause symptoms may go unrecognized.
 
In the interview, Jean discusses how patients may report concerns such as anxiety, disrupted sleep, or brain fog, even when menstrual cycles remain regular, and how these experiences may be attributed to other factors. She also highlights approaches that may support provider-patient conversations, including symptom tracking, written questions, and referral resources for specialized care.
 
Read Jean’s full interview on BlackDoctor.com.

This World Menopause Day, we’re making room for more informed conversations about women’s health and hormone therapy. 

For years, interpretations of the Women’s Health Initiative study shaped how hormone therapy was discussed and prescribed. As clinical guidance evolves, providers are revisiting long-held assumptions and asking a more nuanced question: are we underutilizing a tool that may improve quality of life for appropriately selected patients? 

Our article takes on four misconceptions that still come up in clinical conversations, including the idea that hormone therapy is only about symptom relief.

Today is a win for patient access.
 
The Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee’s recommendation that six out of seven peptides receive Category 1 inclusion is an important step toward preserving a regulated pathway for licensed providers to prescribe personalized compounding medications for patients whose care does not fit a standardized protocol.
 
Empower's focus has always been quality: compounding medications prescribed by licensed healthcare providers based upon individual patient needs, under rigorous compliance standards. Today's outcome means patients and providers are one step closer to accessing peptides within the safeguards of a regulated healthcare system. Upon FDA’s approval of the PCAC’s recommendations, licensed providers can turn to Empower for responsible peptide compounding with confidence.
 
We anticipated this moment. We prepared for it. We are ready.

*The peptide products shown here are not currently available and will only be dispensed if and when permitted under applicable FDA guidance and other legal requirements.

PCAC's first day of recommendations for inclusion are in: BPC-157, KPV, TB-500, and MOTS-c. This marks an encouraging step forward in the ongoing conversation around personalized care and expanding access to patient-specific treatment options through regulated compounding. 
 
The discussion continues tomorrow as PCAC evaluates the remaining peptides under review.
